angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 316,544 km at 9.78 pc = 0.43 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 102.3014 +/- 0.0302 mas (same row, RUWE 1.13): 9.78 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.455 +/- 0.018 solar radii from Maciejewski et al. 2014, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of GJ 436 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014AcA....64..323M/abstract): 316,544 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.47 +/- 0.07 solar masses from Maciejewski et al. 2014, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of GJ 436 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014AcA....64..323M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3505 +/- 51 K from Maxted et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of GJ 436 b's parameter set from Maxted et al. 2022 (the default leaves it empty) in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022MNRAS.514...77M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Maxted et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of GJ 436 b's parameter set from Maxted et al. 2022 (the default leaves it empty) in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022MNRAS.514...77M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/gj-436.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.794, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of GJ 436 (pscomppars): spectral type M2.5 V, from Salz et al. 2015 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015A&A...576A..42S/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of GJ 436 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.0991 dex, from Rosenthal et al. 2021 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021ApJS..255....8R/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of GJ 436 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1.585, from Kokori et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJS..265....4K/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of GJ 436 (pscomppars): age 6 Gyr, from Kokori et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJS..265....4K/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of GJ 436 (pscomppars): rotation period 44.09 d, from Bourrier et al. 2018 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018Natur.553..477B/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of GJ 436 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 0.33 km/s, from Bourrier et al. 2018 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018Natur.553..477B/abstract)
spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (0.455 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 0.632. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
